subject: elephant
pitch: A gentle African elephant calf. Wrinkly slate-grey skin with a dusty, reddish tint from rolling in the dirt, huge fan-shaped ears with a pink flush on the inside, a curious trunk curling forward, stubby baby tusks, long lashes over kind brown eyes, a little tufted tail and round, padded feet with pale toenails.
reasoning:
I'm planning out a calf elephant model as a compact TypeScript module, sketching proportions and a skeleton hierarchy with hips as root, spine chain up to the head, plus trunk, tail, and four leg chains.

I'm working out the coat coloring using layered mottle and stripe functions to give a dusty, wrinkled slate-gray skin, then defining the spine, neck, and head joint positions with catmull paths to build out the body structure.

For the body mesh, I'll sweep along a catmull path from behind the hips to the neck, using the bone chain [spine, neck] so each point projects onto the nearest bone segment and gets proper ownership for skinning.

Now I'm planning body sections with low-poly sides, then moving to the head: positioning a forehead dome sphere relative to the head bone using local offsets for forward/up placement, and adjusting its scale slightly to widen the head shape.

For the trunk, I'm laying out a chain of joints curling forward from the head front, plotting a curved path of points descending then sweeping upward at the tip so it curls naturally above the floor.

Still writing trunk sweep code...

Positioning the jaw box using local offsets from the head bone, then adding a small pinkish box inside for a tongue-like detail. Now moving on to the eyes placement relative to the head.

Adjusting eye position so it sits just inside the head sphere surface, then adding small lash spikes ringed around each eye aimed outward using the head's direction vector.

Now I'm working out the ear shape - a flat extruded outline positioned outward and slightly back from the head's side, anchored at the appropriate local offset.

Writing ear paint logic...

For the ears, I'll attach them as rigid parts on the head via hinge joints named earL and earR, positioned at the ear root with a slight backward tilt, each referencing its own bone.

Now adding tusks as small ivory cones near the trunk base, angled outward and down from the upper jaw, then setting up columnar elephant legs with hip joints positioned wide on the body and foot targets straight below, defining the segment lengths for each leg.

Defining joint naming...

I'm setting parent attachments: front legs off the spine, hind legs off the hips joint, with specific offsets for each attachment point. Now I'm working out the leg sweep geometry with tapering radii and sides for the limb mesh.

Adding foot and toenail geometry...

Checking hip/leg joint overlap looks fine given the body radius falloff near the rear. For the tail, I'm setting up a hanging chain from the rump with a sequence of points dropping down and back for a natural droop.

Now I'm building the tail chain with three segments, a tapered sweep radius, and a ring of small spikes near the tip—oriented with a tilt so they angle outward and downward along the tail's direction.

For the head, I'm scattering sparse dark bristle spikes across the top of the skull surface using a filtered scatter so they only appear where the surface normal points upward, creating a small tuft of hair.

Now I'm layering the body's coloring: a mottled base texture, then subtle wrinkle stripes darkening it along the body axis, then a countershading pass to lighten the belly while keeping the back dustier and redder-toned.

For the smaller details, I'm giving the ears pink roots, the toenails a pale cream color, and the eyes plain brown spheres with a tiny white highlight dot for shine.

Still writing placement code...

Still tuning body radius curves...

Now I'm positioning the trunk root as a child of the head joint, aimed outward and curling up at the tip, then placing a small jaw box just below it using local offsets relative to the head joint.

Widening the ear outline a bit to look suitably large for an elephant calf, then setting ear pose joints and sphere scaling for the head part. I'm adding tusks as rigid spikes attached to the head bone with a base position and direction, plus nail positions on the feet tied to each leg's tip bone, before finalizing the export.

Now I'm defining the foot geometry as a tapered cylinder in a dusty color, attached to the leg's tip bone, and working out how the limb function's bend parameter should be structured for a two-segment leg with one inner joint — passing a single direction array to represent the bend at that joint.

For the leg chain itself I'm using hip, knee, and ankle as the three joint names, with the hind legs bending the knee forward, and lengths of 0.25 each giving a total span around 0.48 so the knee bends slightly forward. That settles the structure, so I'll write it out now.
